newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 29.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul.
Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Bank of Korea forecast long-running business slowdown lasting until late next year. Third-quarter GDP growth rate comes to two-year low at 6.4 percent, as inventories in semiconductors, automobiles soar.
- South Korea-U.S. cooperation in dealing with North Korea is unwavering, president Kim Young-sam says upon returning from his three nation Asian tour.
- A constitutional court rules that the death penalty in South Korea is compatible with the nation's constitution.
- Industrial waste water rise 4.5 times in 16 years: water pollution level is serious as a result of increased use of farm pesticide, according to official environment statistics.

- Mounting number of swindling cases perpetrated by South Koreans against ethnic Koreans in China prompts Korean opinion leaders to join forces in urging the government to address the problem of peope who go overseas and commit disgraceful acts.
- The death penalty is still indispensable in Korea, a constitutional court says in a split ruling.
- OECD chief Donald Johnston urges Korea to expand aid, calls for farming reform, strong central bank.
- Mexican president Ernesto Zedillo arrives in Seoul for summit with President Kim Young-sam.
